To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a software framework for the discrete event simulation of a population moving in the Lexis diagram.

the Lexis diagram and the illness-death model can be implemented in the statistical software R and that the resulting simulation framework is flexible and can be used for various purposes in chronic disease epidemiology.

the software framework allows for the simulation of a population in the face of competing risks and different time-scales and that the framework can be easily adapted to other disease scenarios and to other statistical software.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a flexible and easy-to-use framework for the simulation and the visualization of epidemiological data in the face of different time-scales.
the simulation of populations with a chronic disease.
the simulation of populations in an illness-death framework.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the algorithm and software framework described here are useful for the simulation of the epidemiology of chronic diseases.
the Lexis diagram and the illness-death model provide a powerful tool for the simulation of epidemiological models of chronic diseases.
the software framework presented in this work is a powerful tool to simulate populations in the face of chronic diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a new and flexible algorithm for the simulation of a population in an illness-death-model.
we have developed a flexible and efficient framework for simulating populations in an illness-death framework, where calendar time, age and duration of the disease are taken into account.
the Lexis diagram is a powerful tool to simulate the epidemiology of chronic diseases in the presence of competing risks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a flexible software framework is a useful tool to simulate populations in chronic disease epidemiology.
the algorithm can be used to simulate populations with competing risks, and that the algorithm is implemented in a user-friendly software package, which can be downloaded from our web page.
the algorithm and software framework are flexible enough to simulate the incidence and prevalence of a chronic disease under a wide range of assumptions.
